frontier.hypothesis: The 67th instruction in the copy-store-separator family is a load-delay nop caused purely by local-alloc giving the moved copy $v0 for BOTH its pointer and its value; if the moved copy's pointer can be seated in $a0 (as target seats it at slot 16) its two loads separate and the family lands at 66 with the slot-11 load already in hand - which would be a byte match.
frontier.mechanism: Target's C3 is lw $a0,0xC($v1) at slot 16 / lw $v0,0x8($a0) at slot 18 with the 0x24 store filling the delay slot; every T61-class body emits lw $v0,0xC($v1) / lw $v0,0x8($v0) adjacent and pays a nop. The pointer pseudo of the moved copy has refs 2 and a short span, so it first-fits to $v0 exactly like the +2 halfword value does under R2 - the same allocator rule, one quantity over.
frontier.next_probe: Run tools/ra_solver/local_extract.py text1b --func func_80060A68 (QTYDBG) on T61 and on target-shaped K7, identify the moved copy's pointer quantity by birth/death/refs, and read its allocation order and got value. Then apply the R2 recipe to THAT quantity rather than to the +2 value: lengthen the moved copy's pointer range by placing exactly one statement between its 0xC read and its 0x8 deref (the +2 read and the p10 read are the two candidates that do not themselves move), so that a span-2 $v0 quantity is allocated ahead of it and first-fit is pushed to $a0. Sweep the six insertion points on the C1,C2,S1,S2,C3,P prefix x the five T tails and record build_insns plus the 0x10 load slots.

frontier.hypothesis: On the Y1 spine the +2 read can be brought upstream of the gp store - recovering target's slot-22 $a0 load while keeping Y1's slot-11 $a1 load - if the 0x18 store is SPLIT so that its store half lands between the +2 read and the p10 read, giving a free non-gp separator that the copy store was being paid a nop for.
frontier.mechanism: Y1's only residual is that its +2 read is downstream of sw $v0,%gp_rel(D_800A3478)($gp), which sched2 cannot disambiguate from mem(v1+0x10). Splitting the +0 read from the 0x18 store adds no instruction (the lhu and the sh both already exist and stay in the same statement order), and it additionally lengthens the +0 value's live range so that $v0 is occupied across the +2 value's range - which is R2's donor condition satisfied by an existing value rather than by a gp addiu.
frontier.next_probe: Build the family temp0 = *(u16 *)(*(s32 *)(outer + 0x10) + 0); [read2] ; *(u16 *)(outer + 0x18) = temp0; [read3] with the +2 read fused into its own 0x1A store (S3i) as read1 so that read1/read2 are separated for free, i.e. spines like C1,C2,C3, S3i, S1a, S1b, P, S4, S5, S6, S7, S8 and the permutations that keep a gp addiu inside [p10 read, +4 read]. Measure build_insns, the three 0x10 load slots/registers, and pull QTYDBG for the +0 and +2 value quantities to see whether temp0 holds $v0 across the +2 value's range. Note that this reverses target's 0x18/0x1A store order (slots 23 and 27), so score may rise even where the load geometry is right - judge on load geometry and instruction count first.

frontier.hypothesis: U2's residual seat is the same quantity as K7's but U2 reaches it with one fewer local, so the U spine is the cheaper place to attack the +2 value's $a0 seat - if a donor can be supplied from OUTSIDE the fused statement's (nonexistent) interior.
frontier.mechanism: R2's recipe has always been to place a donor statement between the +2 read and its store. A fused read+store has no such position, but local-alloc only requires that some span-2 $v0 quantity be LIVE across the +2 value's two-insn range and be allocated ahead of it - a condition a neighbouring statement's quantity can satisfy without sitting textually between them.
frontier.next_probe: Pull tools/ra_solver/local_extract.py QTYDBG for U2 and list every quantity whose birth/death bracket the +2 value's range, with its refs, span, priority and allocation order. Then sweep the statements immediately before and after S3i (the p10 read, idx, the two gp stores, the 0x1C store) into each adjacent position and re-read the +2 value's got field, looking for any placement that makes a $v0 quantity live across it. Bank the QTYDBG dumps under tmp/grind/func_80060A68/s19/.
